subject: Recap: Post-demo follow-up & next eval steps for EdgeAI tooling gaps
messages:

Cc: Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@edgeai.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood demo — follow-ups and open items

Thanks for the demo today, Ben. Good conversation — we appreciated the streaming example and the function-calling walkthrough. A few follow-ups from our side so we can scope the internal eval: 

1) Feature parity questions we need answered for our procurement/architecture review:
   - Streaming: what guarantees do you provide for partial-output recovery if a connection drops mid-response? We want deterministic resume semantics.
   - Function calling: how do you handle nested JSON schemas and schema validation failures? Is there a retry or fallback?
   - Structured outputs: we need a way to assert schema conformance programmatically and get confidence scores.

2) Perf/ops tests we want to run against HyperscalerX to compare:
   - 256-token streaming latency under steady RPS (50 RPS) with prefix caching enabled
   - End-to-end function-calling with 3 chained tool calls and ~1.2k token context
   - Structured-output validation rate (percentage of valid JSON) across 1k prompts

Can your team share a short test plan and any scripts we can run? Also please send any limitations (max seq len, quantized model differences, or fallbacks between variants).

Thanks — Olivia

--
Olivia Hart
Director, Platform Engineering, EdgeAI
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@edgeai.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <m.ruiz@edgeai.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood demo — follow-ups and open items

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list, and great questions. Recap from our side + proposed next steps so we keep the eval focused.

Quick answers up front: 
- Streaming resume semantics: we provide an at-most-once token delivery model with an append-only KV cache and resumable cursors. If a connection drops we can resume from the last acknowledged token; we also offer explicit idempotency tokens for request deduping. If the client wants exactly-once semantics we recommend the cursor + dedupe approach in the plan attached.
- Function calling + nested JSON: our function-calling layer supports a schema-first path where outputs are validated against a JSON Schema. For validation failures we expose both (a) the raw model output and (b) a best-effort repair pass (a deterministic cleanup step) — you can configure strict vs permissive behaviors.
- Structured output checks: Redwood Optimize can run batch schema conformance checks and emit per-example confidence scores and regression alerts if conformance drops.

Attached: edgeai-eval-plan.xlsx (high-level steps), streaming-test-script.sh (simple runner), function-calling-cases.jsonl (100 canonical cases including nested schemas).

Proposed mutual action plan (short):
1) Today — Redwood sends the plan + scripts (attached).
2) Tue 11/26 — EdgeAI runs the streaming latency test and returns raw traces (request IDs).
3) Wed 11/27 — Redwood runs twin function-calling regression on our infra and shares results; EdgeAI runs HyperscalerX baseline and shares traces.
4) Fri 11/29 — Joint sync to compare findings and decide blocker list.

Who should I follow up with on your side for the test execution? Also calling out that priyom_das will own the function-calling cases and marissa_cole will own streaming/ops instrumentation from Redwood.

Cheers,
Ben

Hi Olivia / Marco — attaching the function-calling canonical cases and a short README with expected success criteria. A couple of clarifications on the tests we propose so results are comparable to HyperscalerX: 

Test A: Function-calling chain (deterministic)- 1000 examples, each exercise: parse input -> toolA -> toolB -> toolC -> final respond- Validate: final payload must match JSON Schema v1.2; failures logged with raw output + cleaned output from our repair pass- Metrics: pass_rate, median latency, 95th latency, repair-rate

Test B: Streaming resume (client drop)- 500 examples at 50 RPS where client disconnects at random offsets (10-70% into response)- Validate: resumed response equals contiguous stream from server starting at last acked token- Metrics: resume_success_rate, average rewind bytes, end-to-end latency impact

Test C: Structured-output robustness- 1k prompts with expected structured response; measure schema conformance and confidence score distributions

We've included a small runner (streaming-test-script.sh) and instructions to emit request IDs and KV-cache keys so logs can be cross-correlated. Please let us know if HyperscalerX can't provide the same request-level traces — we can adapt the runner to sample instead.

Attachments: function-calling-cases.jsonl, streaming-test-script.sh

Action items assigned:
- Olivia/Marco: confirm test execution window for Tue/Wed and who will send traces.
- EdgeAI: share any constraints (max sequence length, tokenization differences) so we can align prompts.
- Ben: sync call after Fri with exec summary.

Thanks — priyom
